candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 24:4, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD. Cf. Rev 22:2.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful' — Enoch's vision of the eschatological tree of life. The tree restored at the eschaton echoes the Edenic tree (Gen 2:9) and prefigures the Revelation tree of life (Rev 22:2 'the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations'). Tewahedo eschatology preserves the tree-of-life imagery as central to its description of the restored creation; the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok's vision pre-dates and grounds the Revelation development.
